My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-sloping trajectory from the current price level, with the 1-day estimate anchored closely to recent trading activity and technical support levels. At the 1-week horizon, I incorporated a slight positive bias based on the broader trend momentum and the assumption that no major macro disruptions would materialize in the near term. The 1-month estimate extends that gentle upward drift further, reflecting an underlying assumption that the asset continues to trade in line with its medium-term trend, though I tempered the magnitude of the move to account for the natural uncertainty that compounds over longer horizons.

The confidence interval widths were deliberately calibrated to widen substantially as the time horizon extends, which reflects the statistical reality that uncertainty compounds over time. At the 1-day level, the interval is relatively tight because intraday volatility is fairly predictable and mean-reversion forces tend to limit extreme moves over short windows. By the 1-week mark, I factored in the possibility of scheduled economic data releases, earnings reports, or sentiment shifts that could meaningfully move prices in either direction. On the downside, a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a surprise inflation print, a sharp move in interest rates, or an escalation in geopolitical tensions — could produce a correction well below the lower bound of my 1-month interval. A broader equity market selloff or liquidity crisis could also trigger cascading moves that overwhelm typical volatility assumptions. On the upside, a stronger-than-expected earnings surprise, a dovish policy pivot, or a surge in risk appetite could push prices meaningfully above the upper bound. These tail risks are real and should remind anyone using this forecast that the stated intervals, while wide, do not capture every possible scenario.
